rules.title: Notice to Tenant of Residential Tenant Protections
rules.requirement: A landlord of residential rental property subject to the Division must give tenants a written notice in no less than 12-point font. The notice states that California law limits rent increases and that local law requires a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy. A copy of the Tenant Protection Guide must be included. For tenancies existing before June 24, 2023, these were due within 90 days of June 24, 2023. For tenancies commencing or renewed on or after June 24, 2023, they must be included in the lease or in a written notice signed by the tenant at lease signing.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to comply with any provision of this Division shall render void any notice of termination required by this Division.

rules.title: Requirements Upon Termination of Tenancy for At-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: Before terminating a tenancy for a curable at-fault lease violation, the landlord must first give written notice describing the violation and an opportunity to cure. If the violation is not cured, the landlord may serve a three-day notice to quit. The landlord must also notify the Commission no later than three business days after notifying the tenant, once the Commission's submission portal has been established.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to the Division who issue a termination notice for at-fault just cause.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706.
rules.quoted_span: Before a landlord issues a notice to terminate a tenancy for at-fault just cause that is a curable lease violation, the landlord shall first give written notice of the violation including a description of the violation and an opportunity to cure the violation under California Code of Civil Procedure section 1161(3), as may be amended.

rules.title: Notice Requirements Upon Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must give written notice at least 30 or 60 days before the termination date, as required by Civil Code section 1946.1, in no less than 12-point font. The notice must describe the basis for termination, the tenant's right to relocation assistance, and the tenant's right to an offer to renew. The landlord must also notify the Commission within three business days.
rules.key_value: at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property subject to the Division who issue a termination notice for no-fault just cause.
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706.
rules.quoted_span: (1) Notice to Tenant. The landlord shall give written notice to the tenant at least 30 or 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination as required by California Civil Code section 1946.1, as may be amended, in no less than 12-point font.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must provide relocation assistance regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy. At the landlord's option, this is either a direct payment or a rent waiver. The amount equals two months of actual rent, or three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled. A direct payment must be made within 15 days from the date of the notice.
rules.key_value: two months of actual rent (three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled)
rules.coverage_text: Tenants of residential rental property subject to the Division whose tenancy is terminated for no-fault just cause, regardless of income or length of tenancy.
rules.penalty: Any landlord who fails to provide relocation assistance as required by section 98.0706(c) shall be liable to the tenant in a civil action for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages.
rules.quoted_span: (i) Unless section 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii) applies, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.interaction_text: Any relocation assistance required by this Division shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any federal, state, or other local law.

rules.title: Right to Offer to Renew After No-Fault Just Cause Termination
rules.requirement: If the unit is offered again for rent within five years of an eviction under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3) or (4), the landlord must first offer it in writing to the displaced tenant. This applies if the tenant asked for an offer in writing within 30 days of the termination notice and gave a mailing or email address. The tenant has 30 days from receipt of the offer to accept.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property re-offered for rent within five years after a no-fault just cause eviction under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4).
rules.penalty: A landlord's failure to strictly comply with section 98.0706 shall render void any notice of termination required by section 98.0706.

rules.title: Buyout Agreements
rules.requirement: Before making a buyout offer, the landlord must give each tenant a written disclosure of the tenant's rights. Buyout agreements must be in writing and include specified statements. A buyout agreement must be for more than the relocation assistance available under section 98.0706(c); otherwise it is void.
rules.key_value: greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c)
rules.coverage_text: Landlords making buyout offers or entering buyout agreements with tenants of residential rental property.
rules.penalty: A buyout agreement that does not strictly comply with section 98.0707(c)(1)-(4), or that is for less than the relocation assistance owed, is void.
rules.quoted_span: Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c). A buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates this Division and is void.
